instruction: Filter the most recent five emails in Thunderbird's daily folder to find only those that have a CC recipient. Extract the sender name and subject for these filtered emails, then save the results in a two-column report as 'cc_emails.xlsx' on the Desktop using LibreOffice Calc.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('alt', 'tab'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(1)

metadata.explanation: Task requires filtering the 5 most recent emails for those with CC field. Verified from email data: only 2 emails have CC (both from eNotices System for Jan 27 and Jan 28). Evaluator checks Excel contains these 2 filtered emails.

llm_judge_reasons: Excellent verification approach: Cross-validates Excel data against actual Thunderbird mailbox to prevent manual data entry
Correct mbox parsing: Uses standard Python mailbox.mbox() library (line 158) which properly handles mbox format and delimiters
Proper sender extraction: Uses email.utils.parseaddr() (line 169) to correctly parse 'Name <email>' format
Complete coverage: Verifies all instruction requirements (filter 5 recent emails, check CC field, extract sender/subject, save to Excel)
Good error handling: Returns empty lists on failures, checks mailbox existence (lines 104-109), handles parse errors
Correct postconfig: Includes Ctrl+S to save Excel file before verification
Sound logic flow: Excel read → Thunderbird independent verification → cross-validation → expected value comparison
Minor: Date sorting uses sensible fallback for emails without dates (line 115)
